submitter: bugfix_277_required_fields_repair lane — migrations 530/531: the diagnosis_guardian council seat's error_step discipline is factually inverted, and the mirror that copies the seat mangles one of its headings. Both APPLIED and verified at the live column before submitting (this estate reviews config after the fact by design — owner ruling 2026-07-29 §2).
rationale:
A council seat's prompt_template IS its standing discipline: it objects on that text, in every relevant round, against every author. The `diagnosis_guardian` seat asserts that the workflow coordinator 'reads ONLY step.config.error_step' and that 'a step-level error_step is parsed but silently inert (a real, recurring trap)', and it judges plans on clause '(d) does it place error_step outside config (silently inert)'. That is the exact reverse of the code. routeToErrorStepOrFail (platform/orchestration/coordinator.go:3666-3679) checks step.ErrorStep FIRST — its own comment reads 'Check step-level first (parallel to NextStep) — preferred location' — and only then falls back to step.Config["error_step"] 'for backward compatibility'. BOTH are read; neither is inert.

Why this is worth a migration rather than a note: the seat fires on authors who did the RIGHT thing. That is precisely the pathology RFC_022 was narrowed to fix — a signal that fires on the recommended remedy stops discriminating, and reviewers learn to wave the seat through. It was caught and refuted at source during bugs_open/301's round on 2026-08-19, recorded in that lane's handoff as owed ('it will mis-fire on every correct submission until someone tells them'), and had sat unfixed since because 'tell the seat' had no owner.

A second defect surfaced while reading the two rosters side by side, and it is a defect in the mirror rather than in anyone's prose: council-gate's copy carries the heading '## The author's stated rationale loop's load-bearing disciplines' where fix-proposer reads '## The diagnosis loop's load-bearing disciplines'. Cause read at source: 099_SYNC_gate_roster.py:85 does an UNANCHORED p.replace('## The diagnosis', "## The author's stated rationale"), intended to swap the diagnosis CONTEXT block for the submitter's rationale, which also hits any other heading starting with those words. The result is a sentence that parses as nonsense at the head of the list of disciplines the seat exists to defend. 531 repairs the live text; the same task anchors the script's substitution to the whole heading line so the mirror cannot manufacture it again.

The seat keeps every other discipline, its footprint and its non-veto status. The bullet is REPLACED rather than deleted because the underlying concern — a plan that drops or misdirects error routing — is real; what was wrong was the test it applied.

edits.rationale: Two verbatim replacements in one prompt_template on one step. Anchors asserted to occur EXACTLY once each (a second occurrence means the prompt was restructured and a blind replace would edit the wrong one). Forward and reverse are built from the SAME variables, and a reverse-replacement control asserts the result returns to the exact pre-image — so an over-reaching replace aborts rather than committing. Verify block re-reads the LIVE column (not the variables) and RAISEs: ON_ERROR_STOP ignores a non-empty SELECT result, so only an exception can stop the COMMIT. It checks the stale claim is gone, both corrections are present, and — the untouched-neighbour control — that THREE-TIER CITATIONS and TOKEN/POD ISOLATION still exist. Exercised three ways before applying: (1) whole file with COMMIT swapped for ROLLBACK — guards pass, 1 row, NOTICE; (2) anchor pre-broken — aborts 'the CONFIG-LEVEL error_step bullet does not occur exactly once'; (3) 'silently inert' PLANTED elsewhere in the prompt — the verify aborts, so the negative control is not vacuous. Round-tripped with its _ROLLBACK to a byte-identical md5 (cbfcc98131ed001944261d3ceba71e99 len=4248), then applied for real (live md5 now 99bf2e459e3080cb9d99b52a520e1500).

The same two replacements on the gate roster, BY HAND rather than via 099 --apply, which is suspended because it would revert migration 377 across all 17 seats and with it a measured ~68% prefix-cache saving (CLAUDE.md's documented exception; worked pair 381+383). Plus the third replacement repairing the mangled heading. 377 safety: every anchor is downstream of <!--CACHE_BREAKPOINT-->, the marker's offset is asserted unchanged, AND the verify runs the fleet-wide health check (17 marked seats, exactly 1 distinct shared prefix) — which is the guard that can actually fail here, induced 2026-08-21 by prepending text to this seat's prompt: it aborted with '377 shared prefix FRAGMENTED — 2 distinct prefixes across 17 marked seats'. The header states honestly that the marker-offset check is structurally unfirable for THIS anchor set and says why it is kept. Also verified: the legitimate '{{.input_data.rationale}}' context block survives the heading repair. Round-tripped byte-identically (191a7bbc6fb313127caadc2bdb3823ea len=4301) then applied; live md5 now 347a20cfe50cb17856509d08500a3e0c.

plan.risks: A council seat's prompt is read at run time, so both rosters changed live with no roll. A round in flight during the seconds between 530 and 531 could have read one corrected and one stale roster; both are now consistent, verified at the live column. The corrected bullet is LONGER than the one it replaces (fix-proposer prompt 4248 -> 4550 bytes). It sits after 377's cache breakpoint, so the shared cached prefix is unaffected — asserted by the verify, not assumed. This narrows what the seat objects to: it will no longer flag error_step PLACEMENT. That is the intent — placement is not a defect — but a genuine 'this failure path has no routing at all' objection must still be reachable, which is why the replacement bullet names removal and swallowing explicitly rather than deleting the concern. 099's OTHER known defect is untouched and still stands: its transform predates migration 377, so --apply remains SUSPENDED. This change makes the script less wrong; it does not make it safe to run.
